plugins.description: Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Replaces bb's thread list with one Activity list of every parent thread from every project, latest first, with pinned threads above it and the Working, Asleep and Archived shelves folded at its foot. While you have regional managers, a row tops it with a small Managers | Threads icon segment and the shown view's options: Managers shows the pinned ones as a grid of avatars above the rest, listed oldest first by their avatar, name and the first sentence of their latest message, and Threads is the list without them. Each view has its own project filter and a Compact switch for one-line rows. Each row shows the thread's agent, its project's coloured initial, its title, its pull request, how many threads run under it, and its state or how long ago it last moved. Right-click a row for bb's own thread menu, with Sleep (or Wake) added; under the pointer, its corner offers Archive. A thread put to sleep waits on Asleep until its time, then comes back to the top. Rest on a row for its card: its state and since when, machine, project, branch, pull request, its plan while it works, and a tree of its subthreads to open.

Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Run bb threads on on-demand boat.dev sandboxes that stop when idle, resume on the same disk, and start from the boat saved snapshot, environment and size you pick in the composer, with bb's GitHub login or else boat's, see boat spend, running sandboxes and money left in a New thread card, and watch a thread's sandbox desktop live and view only from a Computer card in its side panel.
Wakes your Grok Bots by webhook when a bb thread needs attention: an open question or approval, a finished turn, or a failure.

Cards under the new-thread composer. The first, Activity, is six months of your merged GitHub PRs as a calendar grid, with the threads you started, PRs merged and lines changed; its data refreshes in the background, so it opens instantly. With PR Reviews installed, its pull requests card sits beside Activity. With Burn installed, a Burn card shows your spend and tokens for the last week or month against the period before.

Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Browser-style tabs across the top of bb's main panel, each holding a whole split layout. Clicking a tab brings back its panes at their exact sizes, with the same pane focused; if a bb update stops that, tabs switch with their panes side by side at equal sizes, and the strip says so once. + opens a tab on the New thread screen, and × or a middle-click closes one. Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab step through tabs and Alt+1–9 go to one, all rebindable. Clicking a thread in the sidebar goes to the tab that has it open, and a middle-click opens it in a new tab; Cmd/Ctrl-click still opens it in a split, as in bb. Each tab is named after its focused pane's thread and shows a stack of project tiles, one per thread, with the focused thread's in front. Each window keeps its tabs across reloads, and an archived or deleted thread leaves them. Each pane keeps its own header below the strip.
Agents draw mdxcn figures in chat: callouts, steps, terminals, tables, KPIs, charts, timelines and more, from a fenced block.

Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Jot a note from anywhere in bb: click Notes in the sidebar footer or press ⇧⌘J, and a Notes popover opens beside the sidebar with your notes and a composer at its bottom. Type and press ⌘↵. Type @ to link a thread, and attach screenshots or recordings by pasting, dropping or clicking 📎. Or highlight text in a reply and choose Add to notes to keep that passage with a link back to its message. The same list is a Notes card on the New thread screen. Click notes to tick them, then delete them, or choose New thread to put them in the new-thread composer as context, from any screen; on a thread page, Send to this thread puts them in that thread's draft instead. They stay on the list, marked In draft, until you send that message, which deletes them. ⌘↵ and ⇧⌘↵ do the same from the list.

Experimental: it may break with a bb update. A daily The Office quote above the new-thread composer. One random quote per day from a public quotes API, with the character who said it; the composer and the homepage cards move down to make room.

A PR Reviews app on the left rail that opens in the main pane, keeps bb's thread sidebar visible, and lists your pull requests across every GitHub project, in Authored by me, Needs my review and Recently merged, with stacked pull requests as trees, and opens each one on a page with its whole diff in a file tree and a guided review, written by a review thread, that walks you through the change step by step. Its Summary shows the PR's activity, as GitHub's Conversation tab does, and every diff shows the PR's GitHub review threads where they belong. It posts to GitHub only the review comments, replies and conversation comments you write or pick from the guide, on your click, on a PR you didn't write batches them into a pending review you submit as a comment, approval or request for changes, or submits one with no comments, and changes or merges a pull request only from the state badge and the Merge button on its page; review threads never post to GitHub. A card on the new-thread screen shows the PRs waiting on your review, or your own.
Agents answer data with an inline chart, without being asked, using bb's inline visualizations.

Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Start a regional manager: a long-lived thread that takes on a body of work, plans it as issues, and starts an agent, a child thread, on each issue; all of one manager's agents are its crew. Open its panel in the navigation rail and press New: give it a name, an optional description and an avatar, a still blob in one of 21 shapes and 11 colours, and press Create, which saves it with no thread and opens its page; there bb's own new-thread composer, already set to a fresh worktree and auto permissions, takes its goal, and sending it starts the manager's thread, titled with the name, on what the composer picked, the goal its first message and its GOAL.md. The panel lists each manager by its avatar, its name and its description, the ones not started yet under Not started and the others under their project; a row opens a started manager's thread, and the page of one not started yet, which edits all three, deletes it, and names it in bb's title bar. Above a started manager's composer, its avatar and name open the same editor below them, while a rename in bb's sidebar renames it too and never changes its avatar. It keeps the work in its issues, what was decided about each included, and its notes and your standing rules for it in a folder of markdown files on the bb server. It writes to you answer first and in proportion to the question, and stays quiet on a wake that brings you nothing to know or decide. Each issue is numbered after a key taken from its project's name, as BBP-4 in bb-plugins, and is build work, code verified on its own branch, or research, a probe, spike, investigation or design whose result is a report; it has a description for you, a brief and done-criteria for its agent (for research, the questions its report answers), and a status the plugin derives from what its agents did: Backlog, Todo, In progress, Reviewing, Verifying, In review, Done or Canceled, with Needs you flagged above them when only you can act. An issue can depend on others: it is blocked while one of them is open, derived on every read and never stored, and a dependency that would close a cycle is refused; dependencies inform and never refuse, so the manager can start an agent on a blocked issue, its catch-up lists the issues ready to start, and it is woken when a merge or a handoff unblocks one, while a dependency carries nothing between issues. An issue can be split into sub-issues, one level deep: the parent never has an agent, its status rolls up from theirs, and its dependencies block them; once all of a build parent's work is merged, an independent verifier the plugin starts checks its own done-criteria on the default branch, a final check that makes it Done, while a failed one is the manager's to fix with a new sub-issue. An agent works on its own branch, in a fresh worktree or a sandbox, on the provider and model the manager names or else on the manager's own; when the manager hands an issue to a new agent, the old one is stopped, never archived, and the new one continues in its environment, on its branch with its uncommitted files and pull request, moves the work to a new environment on a branch cut from its branch (through origin, once pushed, when a sandbox is on either side), or starts clean from the default branch, with every earlier handoff and verdict in its first message; the manager also names what verifies each build issue, from the preferences you give it, and the plugin picks an independent verifier when it names none. An agent ends its work with one handoff (done, blocked or gave up, with what it did and its evidence), stored whole. A research agent's done handoff carries its report: nothing verifies it, the issue is Done at once, and the plugin saves the report as a file in the manager's memory, which the manager names in the briefs of the agents that need it; the plugin hands it to nobody. Every done handoff of build work is first reviewed by a reviewer the plugin starts itself, a hidden thread in the agent's environment on a model other than the agent's and the verifier's when bb has one, which reviews the diff as the manager's CREW.md instructs reviewers (the plugin names no review of its own) and reports findings, each with a file, line, severity and claim, while the issue is Reviewing; a reviewer that can't start, stalls or stops without reporting never holds the issue. Then it is checked by a verifier the plugin starts itself: a hidden thread in the agent's environment, on another model than the agent's when bb has one, that runs what proves each done-criterion, triages each of the reviewer's findings with a reason, with anything it asks a person declined, and returns a verdict with the output as evidence, while the plugin itself checks that the claimed commit is checked out on a clean tree. The reviewer and the verifier get the issue's decisions, and work that follows one is never a finding. A must-fix fails the verdict, as a failed criterion does, only when the verifier anchors it: a bug hit in normal use, with the steps that reach it, or a broken done-criterion, requirement the brief states explicitly or recorded decision; it downgrades one that meets none, as a principle or REVIEW.md violation or a bug that needs a contrived setup, and should-fix and nit findings never fail it. A verdict that passed waits for CI when the issue has a pull request. An agent's first failed verdict goes straight back to it as the verifier's message, with only the anchored must-fixes and a count of the other findings that held; a second goes to the manager, which sees every finding with the verifier's triage and reason. When an issue passes with a confirmed should-fix, a downgraded must-fix or a should-fix the verifier found itself left, the plugin files every finding its rounds held without blocking it as one follow-up, a top-level build issue in Backlog that stays blocked until the issue is Done, named in the issue's Activity and the manager's update; nits alone file nothing and stay in the feed. When an issue's latest verdict failed on review findings alone, every criterion passing and CI not failed, the manager can accept it as it is with a recorded reason: it waits In review, "Accepted with follow-ups", until its pull request merges, and the findings it was accepted with, its unfixed must-fixes among them, are filed as a follow-up. An issue gets 3 failed verdicts across all its agents: at the third, and each later one you haven't allowed, nothing goes back to any agent and the plugin itself asks you on the board, leading with why the last round failed; until you answer, the manager can't start or message an agent on it, nor accept it, any answer allows one more round, and the question leaves Needs you once the issue closes. The plugin wakes the manager with a short message, hidden from you, that names what happened and never quotes an agent: on handoffs, final checks, failures, an agent waiting on you, an issue back in Todo or unblocked, pull request and CI changes read through gh, your comments on issues, memory edits, answers and verification switch, and its own reminders. When only you can decide something, it puts a question about one of its issues, with up to five options and the one it recommends, into that issue's feed and on its board and keeps working; the question keeps your answer among that issue's decisions, beside those the manager records on it, and every agent started on it gets them. Its Board, a tab in its thread's side panel, shows the verification switch, its open decisions and every issue in a folding lane per status, each with its pull request and CI, what blocks it and what it blocks, and a card on hover with its headline, sub-issues hung under their parent, each opening in its own tab beside the Board, or focusing the one it has, to what it is about, its parent and sub-issues, what it depends on and blocks, its criteria as a grid of each round's result, and its Activity, filtered to All, Rounds or Discussion: every round, a handoff or a build parent's final check with its review and verdict, folded to its score with the latest open, among the decisions, questions and comments about it, an open question answering it there, by an option or in your own words, an open round's findings, each a line that opens to its claim and the verifier's word, what failed it and what became of it, and quiet rows of words and a time for its agents, pull request, CI and the manager's changes to its plan, from where the record began for an issue filed before it was kept, and at its foot a field whose every comment goes to the manager, which replies on the issue, records a decision or, when it concerns the agent's work and no check is running, relays it to the agent, who can reply there too; it reads again only when its own issue changes. Issue links in chat are experimental, and the likeliest part to break with a bb update: the manager names an issue to you as a link, which reads as the issue's live status glyph and its id, mid-sentence, shows its card from the Board on hover or focus, and when pressed opens its tab beside the Board, from any other thread in a split; without the plugin it is a plain link reading as the id. The board warns when the manager edits files in its own environment. Below it, Memory, a section that folds like a lane and stays folded through a reload, shows the manager's memory files as one row of cards that scrolls sideways, each previewing its file, named under it with its folder, and opens one to read and edit in place, never letting you and the thread silently overwrite each other.

A live strip above the composer that counts the latest prompt's subagents and child threads, plus any still running, and how long they have taken, and opens into one row per subagent that expands to its report and latest steps and opens its full transcript in the side panel or its own thread; a Subagents tab in the side panel lists every subagent in the thread, grouped by the prompt it was launched after.
